No.6960/2010 On The File Of I Additional Small Cause
Judge & Mact, Bangalore, Dismissing The Claim
Petition For Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Dismissal, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 07.09.2023 passed in M.V.C.No.6960/2010.
2.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant.

The case of the claimant is that on 10.05.2010 at about 8:10 a.m., the claimant was proceeding on a motor cycle towards Bommanahalli, Electronic City, near BMTC Bus Depot, Hosur Road, Bangalore, at that time, the offending vehicle came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of the claimant.

Due to the said impact, the claimant sustained bleeding injuries and multiple fractures and he has spent more than an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment, NC: 2023:KHC:33835 transportation,
attendant charges etc.,
because of the injuries sustained by him, there is permanent disability.
According to the claimant, he was earning an amount of Rs.15,300/- per month working as a Supervisor in Electrical Technical Works.

3. When it comes to the liability, the Court below had observed that the accident had taken place on 10.05.2010 and the complaint was given on 22.06.2010 i.e., after 45 days from the date of accident.
The Court has also observed that it is the case of the claimant that he was in hospital till 28.05.2010 and immediately after that, he gave the complaint.

Even after discharging from the hospital also,
there is a clear delay of another 26 days in giving the complaint and basing on this, the Court below has come to the conclusion that there is inordinate delay in giving the complaint.

4. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that immediately after the claimant was admitted to the hospital on 10.05.2010, he has stated before the hospital authorities about the accident and Ex.P.19 - inpatient record clearly reveals that he met with an accident as he was hit by a bike which is at an earliest point of time i.e., on 10.05.2010, and basing on it, it is NC: 2023:KHC:33835 submitted that along with Ex.P.19, MLC Register was also filed which clearly shows that as on the date of the accident itself, in the MLC Register it is entered that it was a road traffic accident hit by motor cycle.
Learned counsel submits that mere delay in giving the complaint itself cannot be a reason for dismissing the claim.
It is submitted that the medical records coupled with the evidence of Exs.PW.1, 2, 3 and RW.1 clearly shows that the accident had taken place.

Mere delay cannot be a Sri Narasimha Swamy J vs The Oriental Insurance Co Tld on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11128626/
2 ground to non suit the claimant.
5.

sentences.text: When there was no representation on the last occasion, the matter was posted under the caption 'for dismissal'.
Today also there is no representation on behalf of the respondent - insurance company.

As this is an appeal of 2010, this Court is proposing to hear the appeal on the merits of the matter.
6.
The only ground basing on which the claim petition is dismissed is that the complaint is filed after 45 days from the date of accident.

The Court below in the entire discussion had failed to consider Ex.P.19 - the inpatient record, the medico legal register wherein, the information about the accident was NC: 2023:KHC:33835 given at an earliest point of time.
In this case, the delay in giving the complaint cannot be a ground to dismiss the complaint.
In view of the same, the finding arrived by the Court below is not correct.
Accordingly, the order and the appeal is set aside and the matter is remanded back to the Court below for fresh consideration.
i. The court below without taking into consideration the delay, shall consider the evidence on record both on liability as well as the compensation and shall pass appropriate orders.
ii. The entire exercise shall be completed within a period of four months from the date of receipt of copy of the order.
iii. Without further notice, the party shall appear before the Court below by 30.10.2023 and it has to be decided within four months time.
As evidence is already on record, basing on the same, the Court shall decide the case.
